frames.subject: Splice, an individual free embodied person maintaining Low Water's workshop and infrastructure, compact civilian proportions within an ordinary human-sized body. Modest narrow shoulders, short practical torso and lean separated articulated limbs. A small horizontal CRT-like face frame wider than tall with two soft amber pixel eyes and a subtle wry mouth, no antenna. Maintained bone painted outer panels over warm dark steel mechanical joints, no large chest plate or fighting armor. One broad rust-colored replacement forearm on anatomical left, viewer right in the front view. Muted magenta wrist band on anatomical right, viewer left in the front view. Low-profile offset tool rack attached at anatomical left rear hip with two secured blunt practical hand tools in closed sockets, not held in the hands, not a backpack or gun. Rack is attached visibly and does not obscure joints or legs. Short utility belt and one deliberate rectangular repair plate, few large seams and purposeful fasteners. Two arms, two separate mechanical hands with four fingers and a thumb each, two legs and two grounded industrial shoes. Visible coherent shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip and knee pivots with real attached collars; no floating cables or fragments. Friendly impatient competence, a scrappy technician who would rather work and hang out than fight. No gun, integrated weapon, peaked cap, army shoulder plates, national symbols, black-red issued uniform, red attack optic, skull face or writing. Do not copy Latch's tall face frame or left antenna, or a broad Union Sweeper silhouette. No dense realistic scratches or random exposed wires; large painted panels and clear hand contacts matter more than surface noise.
